title: fix(verify): os verify writes nothing to an object on an external datasource, even one whose write gate is open
body:
Fixes #35255

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:应用作者对声明了可写外部数据源的应用跑校验时,校验不再往那个外部数据库里写测试数据,报告里把这类对象标成“外部、未演练”,之前会真的插入、改、删测试行。
- 为什么做:校验工具承诺只在自己的临时内存库里写,这次补上外部数据源这个漏口,并把说明文字改成与实际一致。
- 出错会怎样:最坏情况是外部对象少测一项、报告里显示为跳过,不会让校验失败,也不碰任何数据;可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么:无

## What changes

- `packages/verify/src/derive.ts`: `deriveCrudCases` now blocks every object on an external datasource, whatever its write gate says. Before, an object whose gate was open (the datasource's `external.allowWrites` and the object's `external.writable`) got a CRUD case with a synthesized body, and every write family that builds its records from that case (CRUD, RLS, reference shapes, delete behaviours, unique scopes, parent write reach, dashboard windows) wrote to it. The harness connects the app's declared datasources the way `os dev` does (ADR-0062 D1/D2, `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` in `harness.ts`), so those writes went to the real database behind it. The skip reason names the gate's state: `external datasource "NAME" (writes allowed): not exercised — verify writes only to its ephemeral store`, or `(read-only)`. A datasource counts as external the way the engine's write gate counts it (a declared `schemaMode` other than `managed`, or an object with an `external` block), so an object bound by `schemaMode` alone is covered too.
- The seat's ruling (leave external objects out of the write phases, name them external and not exercised, no new flag or interface) is the shape implemented. It reuses the existing `blocked` / `skipped` reporting; no interface changes.
- `harness.ts` header, the quotation of it at the sign-up site, `packages/verify/README.md` and the `os verify` section of `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` no longer say the harness "never touches a real database". They say what happens: its own database is in-memory; declared datasources are connected as under `os dev`, so reads reach them; verify's own writes never reach an object on an external datasource; a write the app makes itself (its seed, or a hook or flow one of verify's writes fires) goes where the app sends it; only `--flow` refuses every write routed away from the in-memory database.
- Two tests used "a write-opted-in external object is NOT blocked" as their witness that `datasources` resolves across packages (ADR-0130 D4): `packages/verify/src/artifact-collections.test.ts` and the option-B probe row in `packages/cli/test/fixtures/option-b-reader-probe.ts`. Both now read the same map through the reason: it says `(writes allowed)` only when the datasource was found.

## Tests

- New `packages/verify/src/verify.external-datasource-no-writes.test.ts` boots one stack whose app declares an external datasource with an open write gate, backed by a driver the suite owns that records every write. It runs the CRUD round trip, reference shapes, delete behaviours and unique scopes over it. The recording driver receives no write, each family's report names the external object not exercised, and the CRUD report lists it `skipped` with `(writes allowed)`. A managed object that requires it is skipped; one that only references it is verified. CONTROL: a write sent through the REST door to the same object does reach the recording driver.
- `derive.test.ts`: the external block now pins read-only, half-open, fully open and `schemaMode`-only shapes, the cascade to a dependent, and a managed secondary datasource staying unaffected.

<details><summary>Ablation (one run, then restored)</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `packages/verify/src/derive.ts`, restoring the old behaviour (let a fully write-opted-in external object through): anchor x1 to x0, blob `d29f7503` to `0aa7a191`. The suite resolves `derive.ts` from source (relative import), so no rebuild was needed for this leg.

- Mutated: `Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3)`. The recording driver received 10 writes (expected `[]`), every one a `create` on `vxn_remote`, from the four families run. The CRUD row read `vxn_remote read-failed (404)` instead of `skipped`.
- Restored: `blob after restore d29f7503 == blob at HEAD`, `git diff HEAD empty`.

This also measures the card's premise: the harness does connect the declared external datasource, and the derived writes do reach its driver. Against a real database they would land.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Not changed, and now stated in the header and docs instead of hidden: the boot is the app's, so a write the APP makes to an external object (its seed datasets for that object, or a hook or flow that a verify write fires) still goes to that datasource, as under `os dev`. Confining every write the way `--flow` does (a middleware refusing writes routed away from the ephemeral driver) is the other shape the card allowed; the seat ruled for this one. Read from the code (the seed loader and the engine's write gate do not gate on verify), not measured.
- An object the app routes to a declared MANAGED datasource (not external) is still written through that datasource. If an app points such a datasource at a real database, verify writes there. Out of this card's scope (the card is about external datasources); read from the code, not measured.
- A managed object that requires a reference to an external object is reported with the existing cascade sentence (`required relational target "X" is not synthesizable`), which does not say the target was withheld on purpose. Wording only.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify exec vitest run src/verify.external-datasource-no-writes.test.ts`. Expect 3 passed, with no write recorded by the external driver.

Read first:
1. `packages/verify/src/derive.ts`, the external branch of pass 1: the only behaviour change.
2. `packages/verify/src/verify.external-datasource-no-writes.test.ts`: the recording driver and the control.
3. `packages/cli/test/fixtures/option-b-reader-probe.ts`: the witness row's new `lost` predicate.

Local readings are in the report comment on the card; CI runs the rest.
